Retrofit first, rip-and-replace never rests on one claim: enterprises that industrialize measurement ship faster and defend it in audit. The pages that follow show the mechanics, not just the claim.

items: Protocol translation (fieldbus → OPC UA/Sparkplug) is the unglamorous heart of every twin.
Calibration and data contracts make telemetry trustworthy enough for models.
Ex-rated environments need Ex-rated engineering: safety discipline precedes sensing.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Ask for the baseline: how was the starting position measured, and who signed it?
Ask for the trail: can your auditors replay any decision the system made last week, end to end?
Ask for the unit cost: what does one decision cost to run, and who owns keeping it down?

blocks.x: We can describe exactly where Retrofit first, rip-and-replace never programs stall, because we have inherited enough of them: contract-less integrations, drift without owners and dashboards nobody alerts on. The pattern exists to prevent precisely these.

items: Every stage has a gate with real stop authority — scope expands on measured deltas, not on momentum.
The operating model is designed first — who decides what, at which gate, holding which evidence.
Evidence is generated while the work happens, so the audit is a walkthrough, not an archaeology project.

blocks.x: Critical assets get instrumented with near-zero production downtime using non-invasive mounting.
